claims.text: PRIMARY (rank 1). Bounded MLE inversion (log reparameterization, 4 starts, seed 0) has validation rel_l2 at least 1% relative lower than the fixed ridge configuration (alpha=1.0). Decision statistic: paired bootstrap over n_val=80 validation rows with identical row indices for both arms in each replicate and both targets kept together; the global Frobenius rel_l2 is recomputed for each arm in each replicate and the ratio rel_l2_phys/rel_l2_ridge is formed per replicate. CI: two-sided 95% percentile interval; the decision bound is the 97.5th percentile of the ratio. Claim holds iff that bound is below 0.99. B=2000 requested; if the harness executes B=200 this is a disclosed deviation, and the Monte Carlo standard error of the 97.5th percentile (bootstrap-of-quantile or binomial approximation) must be reported and added to the bound before comparison with 0.99. Equivalent harness statistic: lower bound of relative_improvement > 0.01 is accepted only if shown to be the same percentile of the same replicate ratios. Per-target rule: if physics is worse than ridge on either target's rel_l2, the claim is downgraded to 'aggregate only' and may not be synthesized as a uniform improvement. Gating: adjudicated only after the required_verification_log exists with items 3 and 4 passing. Scope: this validation split, seed 0, conditional on fitted models; CI covers validation-row sampling only, not training, extra_trees or multistart randomness. This is a method-vs-method comparison on a shared split, not a factor ablation; no attribution to the log reparameterization or any single factor. The physics arm inverts with the generating simulator and known noise (inverse-crime, best case under no model error) against a fixed, untuned, 240-row regressor; the result does not generalize to model mismatch, tuned regressors, enlarged training sets, or 'learned regressors' in general.

messages.question: Q-1
messages.text: Proposal only; no evidence exists yet and none of these claims are asserted. Design rationale: with known IC/BCs, known Gaussian noise (sigma=0.001) and an authorized forward model, the MLE/MAP under a uniform prior is the statistically appropriate estimator for a 2-parameter inversion. Log-space parameterization enforces positivity and evens out sensitivity across the [0.5, 2.0] range. Four multistarts guard against local minima or flat valleys in the misfit, which can arise when sensors couple weakly to one segment. Per-row cost is roughly 4 starts x 30 LM iterations x ~3 forward evaluations (Jacobian for p=2 plus the step), so about 360 forward evaluations per row. That stays far below the 3,000,000 budget for any plausible validation size, and should fit within the 120 s wall-clock budget. Library arms differ from each other only in method and params (same raw features, standard scaler, no PCA, no target transform), so the paired comparisons isolate the estimator. Extra-trees is optional, to save time. Caveats: (1) The objective text says four conductivities but the contract fixes parameter_count=2, target_shape=[2] and 2-element bounds. I follow the contract and flag the mismatch for the orchestrator/critic. (2) Explicit FD with 20 grid points and 60 steps may be near its stability limit at k=2.0. If physics underperforms, the first check is forward-model/data consistency (residual norm vs. expected sqrt(40)*sigma), not optimizer settings. (3) Local Fisher diagnostics, if used later, describe local sensitivity only and are not a global identifiability guarantee.

messages.text:
Status: researcher interpretation, unverified. Nothing below is certified.

What S-Q1-002 measured (validation n=80, train n=240, seed 0, data_seed 1302, shared row_hash):
- Validation rel_l2: physics 0.00553, ridge 0.01010, kernel ridge 0.01485, extra_trees 0.01689.
- Per-target rel_l2: physics [0.00478, 0.00620], ridge [0.00887, 0.01121], KRR [0.01525, 0.01443], ET [0.01724, 0.01653]. Physics is lower on both targets, so the global Frobenius number is not hiding a single-target failure.
- Paired relative improvement of physics, from the harness bootstrap with B=200: vs ridge 0.453 [0.355, 0.522]; vs KRR 0.628 [0.502, 0.704]; vs ET 0.673 [0.580, 0.738].
- KRR vs ridge: -0.469 [-0.837, -0.135]. C-Q1-D was 'contradicted': this fixed KRR configuration is worse than ridge.
- Extra_trees has train rel_l2 of about 1.5e-15 against 0.0169 on validation. It interpolates the training set.

Why C-Q1-A/B/C came back inconclusive: the verdicts were not driven by the effect sizes. The physics and library arms necessarily differ in features, scaler, pca, noise_aug and noise_scale, because the physics arm does not use the feature pipeline. S-Q1-002 did not register those fields as allowed varying factors, so the matching gate failed. S-Q1-003 changes only that registration, the noise_scale normalization (requested 0.0 vs effective 1.0, which is inert with noise_aug=0), and diagnostic coverage: it adds per_target_phys_vs_et and moves the per_sample control to ridge, the primary comparator. Arms, settings, margins and the hierarchy are unchanged.

Two disclosures about S-Q1-003:
- It is registered after the S-Q1-002 values were seen. The amendment does not change any arm, threshold or claim direction.
- The pre-registered B=2000 was executed as B=200. Re-running with the harness bootstrap is a disclosed deviation.

Partial implementation evidence so far:
- fit_report checked 200 training samples and found a residual std at truth of 0.0010068 against nominal 0.001, with model_mismatch=false. This is consistent with the forward model matching the generator: residuals at truth are at the noise level, which is what a matched simulator should give. It does not yet satisfy objection-003's requirement of a noise-free reproduction residual well below sigma.
- The last row's chi^2/dof was 0.93.
- Forward evals totalled 11,515, well under budget.
- The local Laplace uncertainty gave 1-sigma coverage 0.63, 2-sigma coverage 0.97 and z_rms 0.985. This is descriptive and local only.
- verification.intervention_verified and diagnostic_gates_verified are both false.
- The 2-vs-4 conductivity question, the observation time indices, the CFL ratio, clipping, per-row convergence and swapped basins remain unverified. They are requested from the specialists above. Blocking objections 016, 018 and 019 stay open until those outputs exist.

Scope caveats for any downstream synthesis: the physics advantage is an inverse-crime, best-case result. It assumes no model error and is measured against fixed, untuned regressors trained on 240 rows. The intervals cover validation-row resampling only, with no training or seed variation. No conclusion about the 'best library regressor' is supported.
